focus: The validation lane: spec/, rules/, validation/ against their real callers, the dispatch machinery (validator-registry.json + engine orchestrator), and the wired-vs-doc-only classification.
noveltyJustification: 8 of 8 findings are new facts; the registry-divergence thread extends iteration 1 but every specific (live dispatch registry, unwired parity rule, 0-reference scripts, duplicated implementations) is newly evidenced.
keyQuestions: What purpose does each directory under runtime/cli declare, and which real callers (commands, bin, hooks, plugins, workflows) actually use it?
Which scripts-registry.json entries have no matching script, which scripts have no registry entry, and which checks are duplicated (rules/ vs validation/ vs root check scripts vs package.json)?
ruledOut: validate.sh implements the rules itself: it spawns the engine orchestrator which spawns the registered rules
rules/ is dead: 28 of 31 check-* files are dispatched through the live registry

label: Two competing registries: the engine orchestrator reads only cli/lib/validator-registry.json (39 dispatchable rules, runtime/lib/validation/orchestrator.ts:76 + spawnSync at 316/363) while scripts-registry.json (scripts-registry.json:4, self-described centralized catalog for dynamic discovery) has NO reader — registry-loader.sh, its designated reader, has zero callers anywhere in .opencode/.github. Counts disagree (9 vs 39).

README.md:110 declares validate-command-tree-parity.sh wired into spec/validate.sh as the COMMAND_TREE_PARITY rule; observed: COMMAND_TREE_PARITY appears nowhere in the live dispatch registry, the orchestrator (654) carries only an unrelated comment, validate.sh never references it; the actual wired caller is .github/workflows/command-tree-parity.yml.

spec/check-smart-router.sh and spec/sweep-track-roots.mjs have zero references anywhere (repo-wide rg over .opencode + .github, tests and docs included, excluding their own directory) — two dead files; the only caveat is undiscovered string-concatenated dynamic imports, deferred to the iteration 9 import sweep.

PLACEHOLDER_FILLED implemented twice, both alive: rules/check-placeholders.sh (115L, dispatched via the validation gate, sourced-only per post-edit-router.cjs:32) vs spec/check-placeholders.sh (184L, the hook canonical, post-edit-router.cjs:41 + 3 reference docs).

COMMENT_HYGIENE duplicated across packages: cli/rules/check-comment-hygiene.sh runs only inside the validation gate (dispatched) while BOTH the post-edit hook (post-edit-router.cjs:36) and .github/workflows/comment-hygiene.yml:17 invoke the sk-code copy (.opencode/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/scripts/check-comment-hygiene.sh).

Phase-parent detection exists in three places despite the no-reimplementation claim (MODULE-MAP spec/ section): the engine rule (runtime/lib/spec/is-phase-parent.ts:19), a 200L near-duplicate runnable-CLI copy (cli/spec/is-phase-parent.ts, 208 diff lines, no callers found), and the shell mirror (cli/lib/shell-common.sh:48, mandated to agree by speckit-implement-auto.yaml:80); all three agree in code, but the comments, MODULE-MAP and the command contract document the laxer ^[0-9]{3}-[a-z0-9-]+ regex that the implemented ^[0-9]{3}-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ does not enforce.

Six spec/ scripts have no wired caller in any of the five surfaces (commands, bin, hooks, plugins, workflows): upgrade-level.sh, archive.sh, quality-audit.sh, progressive-validate.sh, sync-phase-map-status.ts, check-template-staleness.sh — they are referenced only by skill docs (SKILL.md:534, feature-catalog, manual-testing-playbook, references/workflows/quick-reference.md) and run only when a human or AI remembers.

ARCHITECTURE.md:193 says validate.sh enforces 20 rules while the dispatched registry holds 39 (20 authored_template + 13 operational_runtime + 6 structural) — the printed number matches no plausible reading without qualification.
